text: The principle of structure invariance in HoTT says: if A ≃ B and A has a group structure, then:
choices: B has a group structure and it is isomorphic to A's
A and B are definitionally equal
the group structures are the same up to ua only
explanation: Structure invariance (a corollary of univalence): equivalent types can be freely substituted in any type-theoretic statement. If A ≃ B as types, any structure on A transfers to B via transport along ua(e).
